name: cityhall
summary:
The plan is a double cross: a north–south body crossed by three east–west bars, with two big planted courtyards and smaller courts between them. The wings are 12-storey flat-roofed blocks in beige smooth sandstone, with a grid of 3-block bays of recessed dark windows and about 1 in 6 lit. Every wing ends in a blank 13-storey squared tower, as in the photo.
In the middle, a stepped-up central block carries a floodlit penthouse and masts with red aircraft lights, and every roof is a lit slab deck behind a quartz coping line. The west front on Shifu Road has a quartz-columned canopy, the name, the city emblem and flagpoles, and the camera-facing south and east fronts get the most lit windows and floodlit tower panels. Double-cross civic block: 12-storey sandstone wings with piered dark-window grid, 13-storey blank towers, stepped central block with floodlit quartz crown and red-lit masts. West Shifu Rd portico with lit glass hall, emblem, flagpoles; planted courts with fountains.
Facades, roofs and lights are split by trade so S/E faces and roofs read at dusk. (7 of 7 parts finished)
